newsitem.title: FINLAND: Kemira plans share issue, govt to cut stake.
newsitem.headline: Kemira plans share issue, govt to cut stake.

text.p: Finnish chemicals and fertiliser group Kemira Oy said in a statement on Tuesday its board was proposing an extraordinary shareholders meeting to seek authorisation to issue up to eight million new shares.
The Ministry of Trade and Industry would issue a statement later today on its plans to offer Kemira shares this year, Kemira said.
The government currently holds 72.3 percent of Kemira and has authority to lower this to 50.1 percent.
"The purpose of the share capital increase is to finance growth in Kemira's core business areas through acquisitions or other investments," Kemira said.
Kemira said it will also propose at the meeting to waive the preferential right of the current shareholders to purchase shares issued.
The issue authority would run from September 26 until the next annual general meeting, it said.
Kemira's share capital is currently 1,208 million markka, and it has 120.8 million shares each with a nominal value of 10 markka.
Kemira also said it will bring forward the publication of its January-August report to October 3.
